question.text:
Given
(A) $\mathrm{n}=5, \mathrm{~m}_{\ell}=+1$
(B) $\mathrm{n}=2, \ell=1, \mathrm{~m}_{\ell}=-1, \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{s}}=-\mathrm{l} / 2$
The maximum number of electron(s) in an atom that can have the quantum numbers as given in (A) and (B) are respectively:

solution.text:
(i) $n=5$ means $l=0,1,2,3,4$
since $m=+1$
hence total no. of electrons will be 
$=0$ ( from $s$)$+2$(from $p$)$+2$(from $d$)$+2$( from $f$) $+2$ (from $g$)
$=0+2+2+2+2=8$
(ii) $\mathrm{n}=2, l=1, \mathrm{~m}_l=-1, \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{s}}=-1 / 2$ represent $2 \mathrm{p}$ orbital with one electron.
